meta.name: RPSGT v3 EKG checkpoint supplement
meta.purpose: Provide transparent EKG workflow coverage where the extracted learner bank contains fewer than ten eligible D2B/D3C records.
sourceBasis: Sleep-technologist ECG acquisition, electrode-contact, signal-quality, artifact, and cardiac-monitoring concepts
Broad rhythm-family recognition and patient-first response concepts
meta.copyrightBoundary: These questions are original Sleep Pathways Guild wording. They do not reproduce the preserved legacy EKG quiz, generated strips, textbook prose, figures, tables, or proprietary scoring criteria.

questions.task: Monitor and respond during the study
questions.prompt: An ECG-like waveform begins appearing simultaneously in several EEG and EOG channels while the primary ECG tracing remains stable. What should the technologist do first?
options: Label the pattern as ventricular ectopy
Inspect electrode contact, lead placement, and cross-channel artifact before interpreting the rhythm
Increase every high-frequency filter until the waveform disappears
Ignore the pattern because it is outside the ECG channel
questions.answer: Inspect electrode contact, lead placement, and cross-channel artifact before interpreting the rhythm
questions.rationale: Cardiac activity can contaminate neighboring channels. Verify the signal source and electrode pathway before assigning a rhythm label.
questions.source: Sleep Pathways Guild app-authored EKG supplement

questions.task: Monitor and respond during the study
questions.topic: Loose ECG electrode and electrode pop
questions.prompt: A sudden sharp ECG deflection follows movement of a visibly loose electrode and is not accompanied by a patient, pulse, or neighboring-channel change. What is the best next action?
options: Record the event as ventricular tachycardia
Restore electrode contact, secure the lead, and verify the tracing again
Terminate the study immediately without assessing the signal
Reduce the display size and continue without documentation
questions.answer: Restore electrode contact, secure the lead, and verify the tracing again
questions.rationale: The timing and loose contact support artifact. Correct the electrode pathway and confirm signal quality before interpreting the event.
questions.source: Sleep Pathways Guild app-authored EKG supplement

questions.task: Monitor and respond during the study
questions.prompt: During a sleep study, an abrupt ECG change appears and the patient reports chest pressure and dizziness. What is the technologist's priority?
options: Finish measuring every interval before entering the room
Assess the patient promptly and follow the facility emergency and notification pathway while verifying the tracing
Wait for the pattern to resolve before documenting it
Make an independent cardiac diagnosis and begin treatment
questions.answer: Assess the patient promptly and follow the facility emergency and notification pathway while verifying the tracing
questions.rationale: Patient assessment and facility escalation procedures take priority over completing a detailed rhythm interpretation.
questions.source: Sleep Pathways Guild app-authored EKG supplement

questions.task: Analyze, report, and document study findings
questions.prompt: Which sequence best supports a consistent sleep-technologist review of a new ECG pattern?
options: Name the rhythm, change filters, then assess the patient
Verify the tracing, review rate and regularity, inspect atrial activity and PR/QRS relationships, then correlate the patient and neighboring channels
Review oxygen saturation only, then document a diagnosis
Measure the QRS complex first and ignore signal quality
questions.answer: Verify the tracing, review rate and regularity, inspect atrial activity and PR/QRS relationships, then correlate the patient and neighboring channels
questions.rationale: A repeatable validity-to-context sequence reduces premature labeling and keeps the tracing connected to the patient and the full PSG record.
questions.source: Sleep Pathways Guild app-authored EKG supplement

questions.task: Analyze, report, and document study findings
questions.prompt: Repetitive ECG deflections occur only during large body movements and appear at the same time in several PSG channels. How should this pattern be handled?
options: Treat it as a confirmed ventricular rhythm
Correlate video and neighboring channels, identify likely movement artifact, correct the signal pathway, and document any limitation
Delete the affected segment from the study
Change the scored sleep stage to explain the waveform
questions.answer: Correlate video and neighboring channels, identify likely movement artifact, correct the signal pathway, and document any limitation
questions.rationale: Simultaneous movement-linked deflections across channels support artifact and require correlation, correction, and transparent documentation.
questions.source: Sleep Pathways Guild app-authored EKG supplement

questions.task: Analyze, report, and document study findings
questions.prompt: Which note best documents a clinically important ECG change during polysomnography?
options: Abnormal rhythm observed
Cardiac problem diagnosed during sleep
Record the onset and duration, observed rate or pattern, signal validity, patient symptoms, interventions, response, notifications, and unresolved limitations
No note is needed if the waveform later returns to baseline
questions.answer: Record the onset and duration, observed rate or pattern, signal validity, patient symptoms, interventions, response, notifications, and unresolved limitations
questions.rationale: A complete factual note supports interpretation and handoff without exceeding the technologist's diagnostic role.
questions.source: Sleep Pathways Guild app-authored EKG supplement

questions.task: Analyze, report, and document study findings
questions.prompt: ECG signal quality remains intermittently poor despite repeated electrode and lead corrections. What is the most appropriate reporting action?
options: Report a definite normal rhythm for the entire night
Document the corrective actions, the remaining periods of limited interpretability, and the effect on the study record
Remove every affected epoch from the recording
Replace the ECG channel with pulse oximeter rate and omit the limitation
questions.answer: Document the corrective actions, the remaining periods of limited interpretability, and the effect on the study record
questions.rationale: Persistent limitations must be described transparently so the interpreting clinician understands what could and could not be evaluated.
questions.source: Sleep Pathways Guild app-authored EKG supplement
